speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Since you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress, I need to start by asking about your prenatal and delivery history: Was there any meconium staining of the amniotic fluid, and was there a history of prolonged labor or delayed cord clamping?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Given the prematurity and rapid onset of distress, was there any evidence of RDS or did the baby require immediate surfactant therapy? Also, have you noticed any cyanosis or grunting respirations?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) of the Premature Infant.

The clinical picture of a 33-weeker with immediate grunting, retractions, and cyanosis is classic for surfactant deficiency. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray to confirm the ground-glass appearance typical of RDS.
